extracted.intended_audience: researchers, clinicians, and instrument developers conducting or evaluating inter-rater / test-retest reliability and validation studies
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and applying psychometric and feasibility criteria used to develop, norm, and evaluate clinical/field assessment instruments (inter-rater, intra-rater, test–retest reliability, validity, feasibility, and acceptability). Typically applied by teams validating measurement tools in healthcare and allied fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interrater reliability (kappa)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interrater reliability measured using kappa statistics (Fleiss's kappa, Cohen's kappa, weighted kappa) to quantify agreement between raters (reported as κ values).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kappa coefficients reported with interpretation (examples: κ ranges from .28–1.0; average κ values quoted such as 0.66 or 0.70). Use appropriate kappa variant (Fleiss for multiple raters, Cohen for pairs, weighted for ordered categories). Report confidence intervals when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use ICC to measure reliability for continuous or composite scores (inter- and intra-rater reliability of total / composite scores).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report ICC with 95% CI; compare ICCs across instruments or sum-scores (examples: ICCs >0.8 interpreted as high; AMSTAR ICC 0.84; hospital nutrition composite ICC 0.961). Specify ICC model (single/average measures, consistency/absolute agreement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Percent agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Absolute percent agreement between raters for individual items or overall instrument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report percent agreement alongside kappa/ICC (examples: per cent-agreement >80% for many alcohol-environment measures). Percent agreement can be inflated by chance and should be interpreted with kappa/ICC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test–retest reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Stability of instrument responses across repeated administrations over time (test–retest and/or intersession reliability).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use repeated observations with same observers or same conditions and report kappa/ICC for test–retest; example: OHCITIES used test–retest with two observers and reported reliability generally above 0.80.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intrarater (within-rater) reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistency of ratings by the same rater across occasions (intra-rater reliability).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish by rescoring same materials after interval (examples: rescoring videos after 6 months). Report kappa/ICC and note any raters with poor intrarater reliability; consider excluding outlier raters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitivity and specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: Diagnostic accuracy metrics (sensitivity and specificity) of the instrument or imaging method against a reference standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report sensitivity/specificity for relevant categories (examples: NIRT-HDRI sensitivity/specificity ranged 0.57–0.99). Use appropriate gold standard (e.g., µCT for caries, clinical reference) and provide CIs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Area under ROC curve (AUC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall discrimination accuracy measured by ROC curve AUC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ROC/AUC to evaluate instrument diagnostic performance (example: Nu-DESC AUC = 0.9461). Report optimal cut-off values and trade-offs between sensitivity and specificity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct validity (comparative validity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparison of instrument scores with other established instruments or measures to assess construct validity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare ICCs or sum scores with existing validated instruments (example: AMSTAR compared with OQAQ and Sacks' instrument to assess construct validity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreement with gold standard / reference method
rubrics_metrics.description: Concordance between new instrument and an accepted reference or gold standard method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reference methods (e.g., µCT, confusion assessment method) to compute sensitivity, specificity, and agreement metrics; report agreement statistics and discuss discrepancies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensiveness and practicality (acceptability)
rubrics_metrics.description: User perceptions of whether the instrument covers necessary content (comprehensive) and is practical to use in routine settings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure via user questionnaires (e.g., 4-point Likert), report medians/IQRs, and collect qualitative suggestions (example: users found PharmDISC comprehensive and practical; suggested electronic integration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility (time and resources to implement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical feasibility including time to complete instrument and resource/expertise requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report completion times (example: AMSTAR ~15 minutes; NIHSS telemedicine ~11.4 minutes) and discuss barriers like time expenditure or required training. Consider digital automation to improve feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptability / user satisfaction
rubrics_metrics.description: End-user satisfaction and acceptability of instrument implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess with structured questionnaires and report central tendency (e.g., median Likert score) and qualitative feedback about barriers and facilitators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretability / proportion completely classified
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which items/cases can be fully classified and interpreted (e.g., ratio of completely classified PIs / all PIs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report the proportion of items/cases that could be fully classified (example: 82.9% completely classified) and discuss causes of unclassifiable cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighted vs unweighted agreement considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Choice between weighted and unweighted kappa depending on ordinal nature of categories and whether partial agreement should be penalized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use weighted kappa for ordered categories (examples: weighted kappas reported for HOT environment items and NIHSS weighted kappas). Report which weighting scheme used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category-specific agreement analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Report agreement statistics separately for individual item categories or severity grades because reliability may vary by condition/category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present kappas/ICCs per category (examples: dental lesion categories had kappas from almost perfect to moderate). Highlight items with low agreement for instrument refinement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modified agreement analyses (clinically important disagreements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Analytic approaches that ignore minor disagreements (e.g., ignore disagreements between lowest two severity grades) to focus on clinically important discordance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use modified agreement metrics to highlight clinically meaningful concordance (example: modified interrater agreement increased from 76.9% to 93.5% when minor disagreements ignored). Document method clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rater training and calibration (norming)
rubrics_metrics.description: Structured training, facilitated calibration workshops, and norming exercises to align rater interpretations and improve reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct calibration workshops, apply rubric to sample work, hold guided discussions about criteria and search strategies (example: VALUE rubric norming improved ICCs >0.8 for some criteria). Measure post-training reliability with independent scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardized / pilot-tested criteria and instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of standardized, pilot-tested criteria and instruments to reduce ambiguity and improve interrater agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pilot-test and refine criteria prior to formal reliability assessment; use clear operational definitions and consider piloting across heterogeneous settings (example: lumbar MRI used standardized and pilot-tested criteria).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and management of outlier raters
rubrics_metrics.description: Detect raters with poor intra- or interrater reliability and consider their exclusion or retraining for high-stakes evaluations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report individual rater performance (examples: two outlier raters degraded kappa; exclusion improved kappas). Consider reasons (lack of evaluator expertise vs content knowledge) and remedial actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fidelity to scripted/simulated encounter methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of standardized simulated encounters or videos to control case presentation when assessing rater agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ scripted videos or model scenarios to ensure identical stimuli across raters (example: a scripted intern–patient encounter video used to test ESE forms). Note limitations of simulation vs real-world conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of reference standards for cut-off selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection and justification of score cut-offs (e.g., Nu-DESC cut-off of 3) based on ROC analysis and reference standard comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report rationale and performance at chosen cut-off (sensitivity/specificity), and recommend optimal thresholds for context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility of digital integration and automation
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of potential for electronic versions, automatic linking to workflow, and task management features to support instrument use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect user suggestions about electronic integration (example: recommendation to create an electronic PharmDISC that connects to prescriptions and flags PIs for follow-up). Discuss implementation implications.
